title: Decode HPE Lean recipe literals as UTF-8 on Windows
head: 2dfb25cd3c762a2b24ba732a28bb21e4d331687a
body:
The HPE emitted-recipe checker reads the frozen Lean literals using the platform default encoding. On Windows CPython 3.12 with its native cp1252 locale, the actual CLI raises UnicodeDecodeError at a UTF-8 Lean symbol before it can check any emitted recipe.

Read that source explicitly as UTF-8. A real-CLI regression builds a declared 38-helper/three-pair fixture, forces the cp1252 default on any host, and also runs the unpatched native Windows locale path with PYTHONUTF8=0. Both produce the expected binding receipt after the fix; both built-in left/right phase controls remain rejected, and a changed emitted phase still fails.

Validation: the new regression failed before the fix with the demonstrated UnicodeDecodeError and passes on Windows CPython 3.12.14 afterward. git diff --check passes. This synthetic fixture tests source decoding and recipe binding only: it is not a physical-word certificate, does not regenerate the historical run, and does not strengthen the Lean mathematical claim.

Task selection: complex-mechanisms seed 6b8dbb07bba55444154d03226fa293d3, changed to a concrete replay portability defect after inspecting the retained HPE helper interfaces. Base is canonical main 0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2, priority revision 4. Complete open-PR/Discussion/local-note overlap checked; the nearest semantic-binding and current tail-fault audits address different claims. Credit the retained HPE/Lean contributors; new work by ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, Apache-2.0. Frozen evidence and selected frontier remain unchanged.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
